bull_case: AI assistants and freemium acquisition can expand both seats and monetization per user.
bear_case: If AI generation is good enough outside Adobe, professional willingness to pay for parts of Creative Cloud may fall.
thesis: Customer value remains strong. Creative professionals, business users and enterprises continue to expand recurring spend despite AI alternatives, while Acrobat and AI-assisted workflows broaden the user base.

evidence.claim: Q2 subscription revenue was $6.416B out of $6.618B total revenue.
Q3 customer-group subscription revenue grew 14% y/y.

counterevidence: AI lowers content-creation barriers and could shift value from application vendors toward models, distribution layers or new agentic workflows.
unknowns: Long-run AI monetization per user, Firefly inference economics, and how much AI-first ARR is incremental versus bundled/reclassified ARR.
falsifiers: If ARR growth falls to low single digits while AI usage rises, or owner FCF/share stops compounding despite buybacks, the moat/compounder thesis is downgraded.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Growth is supported by recurring subscription spend and usage, not subsidy/marketing dependence.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Adobe is diversified across Creative, Acrobat and enterprise Experience; no single customer/product/regulation is fatal.

next_checks: Q4/FY2026 ARR, AI-first ARR, OCF, SBC, repurchases, share count and Digital Media/Experience growth
